<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 650 420" width="650" height="420">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Grid lines -->
  <!-- Vertical grid lines (every 0.1 m from 0 to 0.7 -> scale: 700px total width for 0.7m -> 100px per 0.1m) -->
  <!-- Let's map x=0.0m to x_svg=120, x=0.7m to x_svg=120 + 7*70 = 610 -->
  <!-- Let's map y=0 to y_svg=240 -->
  <!-- Amplitude = 50px -->

  <!-- Vertical grid lines -->
  <line x1="120" y1="120" x2="120" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="190" y1="120" x2="190" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="260" y1="120" x2="260" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="330" y1="120" x2="330" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="400" y1="120" x2="400" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="470" y1="120" x2="470" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="540" y1="120" x2="540" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="610" y1="120" x2="610" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Horizontal grid lines (Amplitude +50, -50 and intermediates) -->
  <line x1="120" y1="120" x2="610" y2="120" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="170" x2="610" y2="170" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="240" x2="610" y2="240" stroke="#a0a0a0" stroke-width="1.5" /> <!-- Zero line -->
  <line x1="120" y1="310" x2="610" y2="310" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="360" x2="610" y2="360" stroke="#dcdcdc" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Axes borders / frame -->
  <rect x="120" y="120" width="490" height="240" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Sine Wave -->
  <!-- Wavelength = 0.4m -> 280px in svg. Amplitude = 50px. -->
  <!-- Equation: y = -50 * sin(2 * pi * (x - 120) / 280) -->
  <!-- Let's trace it carefully: -->
  <!-- At x=120 (0m), y = 240 (disp = 0, going down? Wait, prompt says: "It crosses zero going down at 0.25 m, and has crests at 0.15 m and 0.55 m.") -->
  <!-- Let's check: -->
  <!-- Crest at 0.15m -> x = 120 + 1.5*70 = 225. y = 240 - 50 = 190. Correct. -->
  <!-- Crosses zero going down at 0.25m -> x = 120 + 2.5*70 = 295. y = 240. Correct. -->
  <!-- Crest at 0.55m -> x = 120 + 5.5*70 = 505. y = 190. Correct. -->
  <path d="M 120 240 
           Q 152.5 160, 225 190 
           T 295 240 
           T 365 290
           T 435 240
           T 505 190
           T 575 240
           T 610 265" 
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.5" />

  <!-- Axis labels and ticks -->
  <!-- Vertical Axis: Displacement / m (or similar, prompt says: "Displacement on the vertical axis, with only 0 marked.") -->
  <text x="105" y="245" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" text-anchor="end">0</text>
  <line x1="115" y1="240" x2="120" y2="240" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Horizontal Axis: Distance / m, marked every 0.1 from 0 to 0.7 -->
  <!-- Ticks at 120, 190, 260, 330, 400, 470, 540, 610 -->
  <g font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">
    <text x="120" y="380">0</text>
    <text x="190" y="380">0.1</text>
    <text x="260" y="380">0.2</text>
    <text x="330" y="380">0.3</text>
    <text x="400" y="380">0.4</text>
    <text x="470" y="380">0.5</text>
    <text x="540" y="380">0.6</text>
    <text x="610" y="380">0.7</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Tick marks on x-axis -->
  <line x1="120" y1="360" x2="120" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="190" y1="360" x2="190" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="260" y1="360" x2="260" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="330" y1="360" x2="330" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="400" y1="360" x2="400" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="470" y1="360" x2="470" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="540" y1="360" x2="540" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="610" y1="360" x2="610" y2="365" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Axis labels text -->
  <text x="365" y="402" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">distance / m</text>
  <text x="75" y="145" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90, 75, 145)">displacement</text>

  <!-- Point A -->
  <!-- At 0.25 m -> x = 120 + 2.5 * 70 = 295. y = 240. -->
  <circle cx="295" cy="240" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />
  <text x="295" y="272" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic" text-anchor="middle">A</text>

  <!-- Point B -->
  <!-- At 0.5 m -> x = 120 + 5.0 * 70 = 470. -->
  <!-- Let's find y at x=470: -->
  <!-- x = 470 is 350px from start (1.25 wavelengths). -->
  <!-- y = 240 - 50 * sin(2 * pi * 350 / 280) = 240 - 50 * sin(2.5 * pi) = 240 - 50 * 1 = 190? Wait. -->
  <!-- Let's re-verify crests and troughs: -->
  <!-- Crest at 0.15m (225) -> y=190 (-50) -->
  <!-- Trough at 0.35m (365) -> y=290 (+50) -->
  <!-- Crest at 0.55m (505) -> y=190 (-50) -->
  <!-- Point B is at 0.5m (470), "on the rising part before the crest". -->
  <!-- Let's calculate y for x=470: -->
  <!-- Distance from 0.35m (trough, y=290) to 0.55m (crest, y=190) is 0.2m (140px). -->
  <!-- At 0.5m, it is 0.15m away from trough (105px). -->
  <!-- Sine wave goes from trough (+50) to crest (-50). -->
  <!-- At x=470, y should be around 240 - 50 * sin(...) -->
  <!-- Let's use exact formula: y = 240 - 50 * sin(2 * pi * (470 - 120) / 280) = 240 - 50 * sin(350/280 * 2*pi) = 240 - 50 * sin(2.5 pi) = 240 - 50(1) = 190. Wait! That's a crest! -->
  <!-- Ah, 0.55m is crest. 0.5m is BEFORE the crest (coming up from trough at 0.35m). -->
  <!-- Let's check wavelength 0.4m: -->
  <!-- 0.0m: zero going down -->
  <!-- 0.1m: trough -->
  <!-- 0.2m: zero going up -->
  <!-- 0.3m: crest -->
  <!-- 0.4m: zero going down -->
  <!-- Let's re-read prompt carefully: -->
  <!-- "It crosses zero going down at 0.25 m, and has crests at 0.15 m and 0.55 m." -->
  <!-- Let's check if crest at 0.15 and 0.55 are consistent with wavelength 0.4m: -->
  <!-- 0.55 - 0.15 = 0.40 m. Perfect! One wavelength = 0.4 m. -->
  <!-- If crest is at 0.15 m: -->
  <!-- Trough is 0.15 + 0.2 = 0.35 m. -->
  <!-- Next crest is 0.15 + 0.4 = 0.55 m. -->
  <!-- Zero going down is 0.15 + 0.1 = 0.25 m. (Matches prompt!) -->
  <!-- Zero going up is 0.15 + 0.3 = 0.45 m. -->
  <!-- Point B is at 0.5 m. -->
  <!-- At 0.45 m, displacement is 0 (going up). -->
  <!-- At 0.55 m, displacement is +A (crest). Wait, if y=-50 is crest (top), then +50 is trough (bottom). -->
  <!-- Let's check y at 0.5 m: between zero going up (0.45m, y=240) and crest (0.55m, y=190). -->
  <!-- So at 0.5m, y should be above the axis (negative displacement in standard math, i.e., above zero line). -->
  <!-- Let's calculate x for 0.5m: 120 + 0.5 * 700 / 0.7 = 120 + 500 = 620? No, width is 490 for 0.7m. -->
  <!-- 1 unit of m = 490 / 0.7 = 700 px/m. -->
  <!-- So 0.5 m = 120 + 0.5 * 700 = 120 + 350 = 470. -->
  <!-- Let's check my path curve at x=470: -->
  <!-- From 435 (zero going up, y=240) to 505 (crest, y=190). At 470, y is indeed around 215 (above the zero line). -->
  <circle cx="470" cy="215" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />
  <text x="475" y="210" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic">B</text>

  <!-- Direction of travel arrow above graph -->
  <g transform="translate(320, 85)">
    <line x1="-60" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />
    <polygon points="65,0 55,-4 55,4" fill="#000000" />
    <text x="0" y="-12" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle">direction of travel of the wave</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Caption -->
  <text x="325" y="398" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" dy="25">Fig. 9.1</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 680 440" width="680" height="440">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Layout / Dimensions:
       Graph box: x from 120 to 620 (width = 500 px for 0.7 m -> 714.28 px per meter)
       Wait, let's use exact nice numbers: 
       0.7 m spanned by 490 px -> 70 px per 0.1 m.
       x_start = 120, x_end = 610 (width = 490).
       y_top = 130, y_bottom = 370 (height = 240, zero line at y = 250).
  -->

  <!-- Vertical grid lines (every 0.1 m from 0 to 0.7) -->
  <line x1="120" y1="130" x2="120" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="190" y1="130" x2="190" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="260" y1="130" x2="260" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="330" y1="130" x2="330" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="400" y1="130" x2="400" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="470" y1="130" x2="470" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="540" y1="130" x2="540" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="610" y1="130" x2="610" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Horizontal grid lines -->
  <line x1="120" y1="130" x2="610" y2="130" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="190" x2="610" y2="190" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="250" x2="610" y2="250" stroke="#b0b0b0" stroke-width="1.5" /> <!-- Zero line -->
  <line x1="120" y1="310" x2="610" y2="310" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="370" x2="610" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Graph frame -->
  <rect x="120" y="130" width="490" height="240" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Sine Wave -->
  <!-- Wavelength = 0.4 m -> 280 px in SVG (since 70 px = 0.1 m) -->
  <!-- Amplitude = 60 px -->
  <!-- Equation: y = 250 - 60 * sin(2 * pi * (x - 120) / 280) -->
  <!-- Let's check key points: -->
  <!-- x = 120 (0.0m): y = 250 (zero) -->
  <!-- x = 120 + 0.15*700 = 225 (0.15m, crest): y = 250 - 60 = 190 -->
  <!-- x = 120 + 0.25*700 = 295 (0.25m, zero going down): y = 250 -->
  <!-- x = 120 + 0.35*700 = 365 (0.35m, trough): y = 250 + 60 = 310 -->
  <!-- x = 120 + 0.55*700 = 505 (0.55m, crest): y = 250 - 60 = 190 -->
  <!-- Let's plot cleanly using a smooth SVG path -->
  <path d="M 120 250 
           C 155 150, 195 190, 225 190 
           C 255 190, 270 250, 295 250 
           C 320 250, 335 310, 365 310 
           C 395 310, 435 250, 470 250 
           C 505 250, 475 190, 505 190 
           C 535 190, 575 310, 610 310" 
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.5" />
  <!-- Wait, let's use exact standard sine curve via standard trigonometric sampling or exact cubic beziers for a pure sine wave: -->
  <!-- Standard sine: y = 250 - 60 * sin((x - 120) * 2 * pi / 280) -->
  <path d="M 120 250 
           C 142 185, 172 190, 225 190 
           C 255 190, 272 245, 295 250 
           C 318 255, 335 310, 365 310 
           C 395 310, 427 255, 435 250 
           C 458 235, 475 190, 505 190 
           C 535 190, 568 305, 575 310
           C 588 320, 600 270, 610 250"
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" display="none" />

  <!-- Let's plot a mathematically precise sine wave using a polyline or smooth path with many control points -->
  <!-- x from 120 to 610 -->
  <path d="M 120 250
           Q 152.5 137, 185 190
           T 250 250
           T 315 310
           T 380 250
           T 445 190
           T 510 250
           T 575 310
           T 610 286"
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.2" display="none" />

  <!-- Let's write out exact SVG path using precise points for y = 250 - 60*sin(th): -->
  <!-- th=0: (120, 250) -->
  <!-- th=pi/2 (0.1m, 190px): (190, 190) -->
  <!-- th=pi (0.2m, 260px): (260, 250) -->
  <!-- th=3pi/2 (0.3m, 330px): (330, 310) -->
  <!-- th=2pi (0.4m, 400px): (400, 250) -->
  <!-- th=5pi/2 (0.5m, 470px): (470, 190) -->
  <!-- th=3pi (0.6m, 540px): (540, 250) -->
  <!-- th=7pi/2 (0.7m, 610px): (610, 310) -->
  <path d="M 120 250 
           C 143.3 190, 166.6 190, 190 190 
           C 213.3 190, 236.6 250, 260 250 
           C 283.3 250, 306.6 310, 330 310 
           C 353.3 310, 376.6 250, 400 250 
           C 423.3 250, 446.6 190, 470 190 
           C 493.3 190, 516.6 250, 540 250 
           C 563.3 250, 586.6 310, 610 310" 
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.3" />

  <!-- Axis labels and ticks -->
  <text x="105" y="255" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" text-anchor="end">0</text>
  <line x1="115" y1="250" x2="120" y2="250" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Horizontal Axis Ticks and Numbers -->
  <g font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">
    <text x="120" y="390">0</text>
    <text x="190" y="390">0.1</text>
    <text x="260" y="390">0.2</text>
    <text x="330" y="390">0.3</text>
    <text x="400" y="390">0.4</text>
    <text x="470" y="390">0.5</text>
    <text x="540" y="390">0.6</text>
    <text x="610" y="390">0.7</text>
  </g>

  <line x1="120" y1="370" x2="120" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="190" y1="370" x2="190" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="260" y1="370" x2="260" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="330" y1="370" x2="330" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="400" y1="370" x2="400" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="470" y1="370" x2="470" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="540" y1="370" x2="540" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="610" y1="370" x2="610" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Axis Titles -->
  <text x="365" y="415" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">distance / m</text>
  <text x="75" y="150" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90, 75, 150)">displacement</text>

  <!-- Point A -->
  <!-- At 0.25 m -> x = 120 + 0.25 * 700 = 295. Let's find y at x=295 on our cubic bezier curve segment from x=260 to x=330 -->
  <!-- At x=295 (midway between 260 and 330): y should be exactly 250 (since it crosses zero going down at 0.25m). -->
  <circle cx="295" cy="250" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />
  <text x="283" y="275" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic">A</text>

  <!-- Point B -->
  <!-- At 0.5 m -> x = 120 + 0.5 * 700 = 470. On the rising part before the crest (crest is at 0.55m / 505px). -->
  <!-- At x=470, y on our curve segment from 400 (y=250) to 540 (y=250) through crest at 470 (y=190)? Wait! -->
  <!-- Let's check crest position: crest is at 0.55 m (x = 505). -->
  <!-- Zero is at 0.4 m (x = 400) and 0.6 m (x = 540). -->
  <!-- So from x = 400 to x = 540 is one full half-wave (trough to crest to zero? No, from 0.4m (zero going up) to 0.6m (zero going down) through crest at 0.55m). -->
  <!-- Let's check coordinates at x = 470 (0.5m): it's between x=400 (y=250) and x=505 (y=190, crest). -->

  <circle cx="470" cy="215" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 680 440" width="680" height="440">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Layout / Dimensions:
       Graph box: x from 120 to 610 (width = 490 px for 0.7 m -> 70 px per 0.1 m).
       y from 130 to 370 (height = 240 px, zero line at y = 250).
       Wavelength = 0.4 m -> 280 px.
       Amplitude = 60 px.
  -->

  <!-- Vertical grid lines (every 0.1 m from 0 to 0.7) -->
  <line x1="120" y1="130" x2="120" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="190" y1="130" x2="190" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="260" y1="130" x2="260" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="330" y1="130" x2="330" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="400" y1="130" x2="400" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="470" y1="130" x2="470" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="540" y1="130" x2="540" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="610" y1="130" x2="610" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Horizontal grid lines -->
  <line x1="120" y1="130" x2="610" y2="130" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="190" x2="610" y2="190" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="250" x2="610" y2="250" stroke="#b0b0b0" stroke-width="1.5" /> <!-- Zero line -->
  <line x1="120" y1="310" x2="610" y2="310" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />
  <line x1="120" y1="370" x2="610" y2="370" stroke="#e0e0e0" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Graph frame -->
  <rect x="120" y="130" width="490" height="240" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Pure Sine Wave -->
  <!-- Formula: y = 250 - 60 * sin(2 * pi * (x - 120) / 280)
       Let's verify key points from prompt:
       - Wavelength = 0.4 m (280 px)
       - Crests at 0.15 m (x = 225) and 0.55 m (x = 505) -> y = 190
       - Crosses zero going down at 0.25 m (x = 295) -> y = 250
       - Trough at 0.35 m (x = 365) -> y = 310
       - Point A at 0.25 m -> x = 295, y = 250
       - Point B at 0.5 m -> x = 470, y = 250 - 60 * sin(2 * pi * 350 / 280) = 250 - 60 * sin(2.5 pi) = 250 - 60 = 190? Wait!
         Let's check phase at x = 470:
         Distance from start = 470 - 120 = 350 px.
         350 / 280 = 1.25 wavelengths = 5/4 lambda.
         At 1.25 lambda, a sine wave starting at 0 (going up/down?)
         Let's check equation: y = -A sin(2 pi x / lambda).
         If y(0) = 0 and going DOWN: y = -60 * sin(2 * pi * x / 280).
         At x = 225 (0.15 m): -60 * sin(2 pi * 225 / 280) = -60 * sin(1.607 pi) = -60 * sin(0.607 pi) approx -60 * 0.97 (not quite -60).
         Let's shift phase so crests, troughs, and zero-crossings match the prompt's exact specs:
         "It crosses zero going down at 0.25 m, and has crests at 0.15 m and 0.55 m."
         Let's define exact sine wave matching this:
         At x = 120 (0.0 m), let phase be phi.
         We want y = 250 - 60 * sin( (2 * pi / 280) * (x - 120) + phi ).
         Crest at x = 225 (0.15 m) -> sin(...) = 1 -> (2*pi/280)*(105) + phi = pi/2 => 0.75 pi + phi = 0.5 pi => phi = -0.25 pi (-45 deg).
         Let's test this formula: y = 250 - 60 * sin( (2 * pi / 280) * (x - 120) - pi / 4 ).
         - At x = 120 (0.0 m): 250 - 60 * sin(-pi/4) = 250 - 60 * (-0.707) = 292 (trough area? wait, let's check).
         Let's construct the standard sine wave path directly using SVG cubic beziers that pass through exact analytical points:
         Points:
         (120, 250) -> zero
         (155, 200) -> going up towards crest? No, crest at 0.15m (x=225, y=190).
         Let's plot standard sine wave starting at x=120 with y=250 going up?
         Wait, if crest is at 0.15m, then from 0.0m to 0.15m it goes up. So at x=120, y=250 and slope is positive (going UP to crest at 0.15m).
         Then at 0.25m (x=295), it crosses zero going DOWN!
         Let's check: from crest at 0.15m (y=190) to zero at 0.25m (y=250), it goes down. Perfect!
         Then trough at 0.35m (x=365, y=310).
         Then zero going up at 0.45m (x=435, y=250).
         Then crest at 0.55m (x=505, y=190).
         Then zero going down at 0.65m (x=575, y=250).
         Let's check if this is a standard clean sine wave:
         Wavelength = 0.4 m (280 px). Amplitude = 60 px.
         Equation: y = 250 - 60 * sin(2 * pi * (x - 120 - 40) / 280) -> let's use exact SVG smooth path (M ... Q ... T ...):
  -->
  <path d="M 120 250
           Q 152.5 160, 185 190
           T 255 250
           T 325 310
           T 395 250
           T 465 190
           T 535 250
           T 605 310
           T 610 304"
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.2" />

  <!-- Let's refine the path using precise cubic Bézier curves for an immaculate sine wave: -->
  <!-- Zero at 120, crest at 225 (y=190), zero down at 295 (y=250), trough at 365 (y=310), zero up at 435 (y=250), crest at 505 (y=190), zero down at 575 (y=250), ends at 610. -->
  <path d="M 120 250 
           C 152 165, 193 190, 225 190 
           C 257 190, 263 250, 295 250 
           C 327 250, 333 310, 365 310 
           C 397 310, 403 250, 435 250 
           C 467 250, 473 190, 505 190 
           C 537 190, 543 250, 575 250 
           C 595 250, 605 280, 610 292" 
        fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2.2" />

  <!-- Axis labels and ticks -->
  <text x="105" y="255" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" text-anchor="end">0</text>
  <line x1="115" y1="250" x2="120" y2="250" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Horizontal Axis Ticks and Numbers -->
  <g font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">
    <text x="120" y="390">0</text>
    <text x="190" y="390">0.1</text>
    <text x="260" y="390">0.2</text>
    <text x="330" y="390">0.3</text>
    <text x="400" y="390">0.4</text>
    <text x="470" y="390">0.5</text>
    <text x="540" y="390">0.6</text>
    <text x="610" y="390">0.7</text>
  </g>

  <line x1="120" y1="370" x2="120" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="190" y1="370" x2="190" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="260" y1="370" x2="260" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="330" y1="370" x2="330" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="400" y1="370" x2="400" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="470" y1="370" x2="470" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="540" y1="370" x2="540" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <line x1="610" y1="370" x2="610" y2="375" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

  <!-- Axis Titles -->
  <text x="365" y="415" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">distance / m</text>
  <text x="75" y="150" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90, 75, 150)">displacement</text>

  <!-- Point A -->
  <!-- At 0.25 m -> x = 120 + 0.25 * 700 = 295. y = 250 (crosses zero going down). -->
  <circle cx="295" cy="250" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />
  <text x="283" y="275" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic">A</text>

  <!-- Point B -->
  <!-- At 0.5 m -> x = 120 + 0.5 * 700 = 470. On the rising part before the crest at 0.55m (505 px). -->
  <!-- At x = 470, y is between zero up (435, 250) and crest (505, 190). Let's place it nicely on the curve at x = 470 -> y ≈ 210. -->
  <circle cx="470" cy="210" r="4.5" fill="#000000" />
  <text x="482" y="205" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic">B</text>

  <!-- Direction of travel arrow above graph -->
  <g transform="translate(345, 80)">
    <line x1="-80" y1="0" x2="80" y2="0" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />
    <polygon points="85,0 75,-4 75,4" fill="#000000" />
    <text x="0" y="-12" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle">direction of travel of the wave</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Caption -->
  <text x="365" y="432" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle">Fig. 9.1</text>
</svg>
